text:
1. He made the border a real border again. In a matter of months, Trump reduced illegal border crossings to their lowest level in half a century. Catch-and-release is finished. The wall is going up and even being expanded, “Remain in Mexico” is back, and the Administration reduced releases into the country by an incredible 99.9 percent.

2. He reversed mass migration. America recorded negative net migration in 2025 for the first time in at least half a century. So far, nearly 3 million illegal aliens have left the country, whether voluntarily or involuntarily: more than 675,000 forcibly deported and the rest “self-deported.” Many of those self-deportations were facilitated by the President’s innovative program to offer plane tickets and cash bonuses for illegals to leave, not only incentivizing good behavior but significantly reducing the cost of deportations. Citizenship and the law actually mean something again.

3. He signed the Laken Riley Act — and required detention of criminal illegal aliens. Named for an innocent girl murdered by an illegal alien, the Laken Riley Act requires federal authorities to detain illegals arrested for theft, burglary, shoplifting, assaulting police, or any crime causing death or serious injury. It also lets states sue officials who refuse to enforce it. Laken Riley should still be alive. This law will prevent tragedies like hers.

4. History’s biggest drop in violent crime, and the lowest violent crime rate in 126 years. According to FBI data, violent crime in America dropped an incredible 9.7 percent in 2025 — the largest one-year decline in history. Murder fell 18.1 percent, robbery fell 18.5 percent. And America’s violent crime rate is its lowest since 1900. This is what happens when you put the National Guard on the streets in crime-ridden blue cities: fewer victims, safer streets, and better futures for America’s poorest.
Trump Launched an American Industrial Supercycle

5. He made the 2017 tax cuts permanent…and better. The One Big Beautiful Bill locked in the largest tax cut in modern history, including the doubled standard deduction, the expanded Child Tax Credit, and 100 percent expensing for factories and equipment. It also delivered No Tax on Tips, No Tax on Overtime, an abolition of most taxes on Social Security benefits, and major relief for seniors. Every Democrat voted no. With the 2017 act set to expire in December 2025, that would have resulted in the largest tax hike in American history.

6. He repealed 129 regulations for every new one. In fiscal 2025, federal agencies finalized 646 deregulatory actions and just five regulatory actions: 129-to-1, and in nearly every case, the “one” was to repeal the others! OIRA says the savings exceeded those of Trump’s entire first term. That is more freedom, lower costs, and less bureaucratic sabotage. Of these, the crown jewel was the repeal of Obama’s 2009 “Endangerment Finding”, the legal foundation for the Green New Scam’s vehicle mandates. EPA calls it the largest deregulatory action in American history and estimates that by itself, it will save Americans more than $1.3 trillion. Trump also killed the federal EV mandate, restored Americans’ freedom to buy the cars and trucks they actually want, and even eliminated the incentives behind the almost universally hated start-stop button.

7. He secured $18 trillion in announced investment commitments. That’s nearly two-thirds the size of the entire American economy, building American factories, chip plants, data centers, energy projects, steel mills, shipyards, and supply chains employing American workers. Apple, Meta, NVIDIA, Micron, Hyundai, U.S. Steel, Ford, Taiwan Semiconductor, and many corporations and sovereign wealth funds are betting big on Trump’s America. No President has ever done anything remotely like it. And it’s just getting started.

8. He made “reshoring” and “reindustrialization” real, not a slogan. Ford is moving Lincoln production out of China. Toyota is shifting Tacoma production from Mexico to Texas. GM, Honda, Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, and others are expanding U.S. production. The capital equipment pouring into the country is the machinery that’s building the growing boom.

9. He replaced lopsided trade deals with balanced, reciprocal trade. Trump used tariffs as leverage to reverse 80 years of lopsided trade deals that favored everyone but America, and to win new or improved agreements with trading partners accounting for more than half of global GDP. Those agreements open foreign markets, attack non-tariff barriers, defend strategic industries, and make it more profitable to build in America than to export American jobs.

10. He shifted global energy dominance from the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of America. Once the world’s largest energy importer — “exporting” $700 billion a year to our enemies — America now outproduces Saudi Arabia and Russia combined. The U.S. is also setting new records in oil, natural gas, and LNG exports, becoming the first country ever to export more than 100 million metric tons of LNG in a year. Trump also opened land, accelerated permits, expanded pipelines and export terminals, and made American energy a tool for prosperity and peace.

11. After four decades of nuclear paralysis, Trump brought five new reactors online in a single year. For more than 40 years, not one new privately developed non-light-water reactor reached criticality in America. Trump ordered at least three by July 4, 2026. DOE delivered four by the deadline, then a fifth just one month later. Decades of zero. One Trump summer: five. That is a genuine nuclear renaissance.
Trump Made Elections Matter Again

12. He broke the Deep State’s power to defy the elected branches. In Trump v. Slaughter, the Supreme Court ruled for the first time in 90 years that Article 2, Section 1 is still part of the Constitution: the President may fire subordinate officials in the executive branch, overturning the 1935 precedent that insulated “independent” agencies from voters’ control. Ever wonder why elections often seem to change nothing? How about one President and 5,000 political appointees vs. 2.8 million unfireable, unaccountable bureaucrats? THAT is the “Deep State”. Trump then made that victory real. For the first time in a century, all policy-making bureaucrats can now be fired for misconduct, incompetence, or defying lawful directives. The permanent bureaucracy no longer gets to veto the voters.

13. He ended nationwide injunction abuse. In Trump v. CASA, the Supreme Court sharply limited nationwide injunctions. A single, local, district judge should not be able to block a national policy for everyone, everywhere; and yet that’s exactly what they’ve done, nonstop, ever since Trump (and only Trump) took office in 2017. In restricting that unconstitutional power, the Court kneecapped the Black Robe Bureaucracy’s favorite tool of unlawful judicial supremacy.

14. He shut down USAID as a left-wing slush fund and shadow government. USAID had become a taxpayer-funded machine for exporting abortion, gender ideology, censorship, and left-wing politics. It had a bigger budget than the CIA and the State Department combined, absolutely no accountability whatsoever, and a penchant for overthrowing governments. Trump terminated it — completely — and moved real humanitarian aid under the State Department. Immediately, seven socialist Latin American governments lost re-election. Coincidence?

15. He shrank Federal employment to its lowest level in 60 years. From a high under Biden, the federal workforce is now its smallest since 1966. Workforce reductions, agency closures, and spending cancellations mean fewer bureaucrats paid to resist the voters. What’s more, when Biden left office, 94 percent of federal employees “worked” from home. The Trump administration cracked down: as Elon Musk put it, “you can work from the office or you can pretend to work somewhere else.”

16. He expelled DEI from the federal government. Trump eliminated federal DEI offices and barred race- and sex-based preferences across the executive branch. Government hiring and contracting are returning to merit and equality under the law, ending the grotesque Democrat idea that “fighting discrimination” requires the federal government to discriminate.
He Defended Faith and Family

17. He delivered sweeping pro-life reform. In his first term, Trump delivered the judges that overturned the abominable Roe v. Wade. Hardly anyone believed it could be done, or that Trump would do it. But he did, and a half-century nightmare finally ended. Since returning to office, Trump has enforced the Hyde Amendment prohibiting the use of federal funds to pay for abortions, reinstated and expanded the Mexico City Policy prohibiting federal funding of foreign abortions, ended federal fetal-tissue research, strengthened conscience protections, protected Medicaid from funding large abortion providers, and pardoned 23 pro-life activists prosecuted by Biden’s weaponized Justice Department. He’s also done everything within the Executive Branch’s power to defund Planned Parenthood. It would be nice if Congress did likewise. No President has ever done more to protect life. No one.

18. He got men out of women’s sports, and restored biological reality to federal policy. The United States government once again officially recognizes two sexes: male and female. Trump ended federal support for the chemical and surgical gender mutilation of children, stopped taxpayer funding of such irreversible abominations, and forced more than three dozen health systems to end or suspend their programs as well. Trump also enforced Title IX as written: women and girls deserve their own teams, trophies, scholarships, and locker rooms. The NCAA and other athletic organizations changed their rules in response. After years of Democrats doing everything they could to destroy women’s sports and ruin girls’ lives, Trump’s administration protects women and girls again.

19. He enacted America’s first nationwide school-choice program — and launched Trump Accounts. As part of the President’s One Big Beautiful Bill, Trump enacted America’s first-ever nationwide school choice program. The new Education Freedom Tax Credit helps fund scholarships for tuition, books, and other educational costs. That’s on top of the new Trump Accounts, which give every child a tax-advantaged stake in America’s future, including a $1,000 federal seed for eligible newborns. Parents gain power. Bureaucracies lose it. And children learn first-hand about free markets and future orientation.

20. He targeted anti-Christian bias and discrimination. Trump created the White House Faith Office, Religious Liberty Commission, and Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias. He restored conscience protections and made clear that Christians do not surrender their First Amendment rights merely by entering public life.
He Restored Peace Through Strength and Put America First

21. He forced NATO to stop freeloading and increase defense spending by 250 percent. For decades, wealthy European governments underfunded their militaries, effectively sending America the bill and using American taxpayers to subsidize their bloated welfare states. Trump forced NATO to replace its old two-percent-of-GDP spending target with an enormous five percent by 2035. Allied spending is rising, American defense orders are soaring, and Europe is becoming a partner instead of a dependent.

22. He drove China out of the Caribbean. China spent years building strategic beachheads at both ends of the Panama Canal, in Cuba, and in Maduro’s Venezuela. Trump forced Panama out of Belt and Road, expanded American security access around the Canal, and captured Maduro, who now sits in a New York jail cell awaiting trial. Beijing’s planned encirclement of the United States collapsed. The Monroe Doctrine is back. Call it the Donroe Doctrine.

23. He brokered eight peace deals in just eight months. In eight months, Trump brokered peace in eight conflicts spanning four continents, including wars that had gone on for as much as 40 years. It’s a record unmatched by any other President.

24. He launched and funded Golden Dome, the first-ever true missile defense for the U.S. population. Ronald Reagan dreamed of making nuclear missiles obsolete through his Strategic Defense Initiative. Today, Trump is actually building it: a layered homeland shield with space-based sensors and interceptors, conventional defenses, and new technologies including microwave systems to destroy drone swarms and directed-energy weapons (yes, lasers) that can replace an $11 million missile with $2 of electricity. Congress has funded the initial $25 billion, with far more on the way once it passes the NDAA this fall. Better a shield than a sword.

25. He restored the warrior ethos — and reversed the recruiting crisis. After years of missed targets under Biden, every active military component met or exceeded its 2025 recruiting goal. Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth refocused the newly renamed Department of War on actually winning wars, while pouring resources into shipbuilding, munitions, drones, missile defense, and America’s atrophied industrial base. Young Americans once again believe their Commander-in-Chief is worth serving. And they’re showing up en masse.

text:
The desire of young men for a people, a place, and a future that is recognizably theirs is not a modern invention. It is as old as the reasons men first left the state of nature. They did so not to dissolve every particular bond, but to secure life, liberty, and the property that sustains both, by mutual consent under known laws. A political community that systematically tells one portion of its sons they may have no exclusive claim to the land, the language, the institutions, or the inheritance their fathers built, while granting those same claims to others by mere presence or birth, ceases to be a community of consent. It becomes a holding pen.

The Fourteenth Amendment, read as an open-ended guarantee of membership to anyone born on the soil, has been stretched far beyond any original understanding of consent or mutual protection. Locke was clear: political society is entered by agreement, not by geography alone. Parents transmit to their children the rights and obligations of that society; they do not thereby obligate the society to absorb unlimited numbers whose formation, loyalties, and numbers may later make the original compact unworkable. When the scale of entry exceeds the capacity of existing citizens to maintain the security of their persons and estates, the contract is strained. The remedy is not to pretend the strain does not exist, nor to sermonize that every particular people must dissolve into a universal one. The remedy is to restore the principle that membership is a political act of consent, not an automatic consequence of location.

Religious language that treats every claim to a particular homeland as sinful simply relocates the same problem. It offers young men duties without corresponding rights of inheritance, and calls the resulting resentment a failure of faith. A government, or a church, that cannot or will not distinguish between the protection of its own members and the open-ended claims of outsiders will eventually lose the loyalty of those members. Men will then seek their security outside the law. That outcome is neither mysterious nor inevitable; it is the predictable result of a political society that forgets why it was formed.

1 Corinthians 10:26 - Creation Belongs to the Lord

God offers total ownership and sovereign control over all creation. He presents every creature and resource on earth as His good gift, free from defilement by false gods or idols.

Our Response should be to enjoy His gifts with a clear conscience and deep thanksgiving. We exercise our Christian liberty responsibly, using creation to honor Him while refusing to cause fellow believers to stumble.

God promises that His absolute ownership protects creation from spiritual contamination. He guarantees that everything received with gratitude remains sanctified for those who belong to Him.

Key Takeaways
•Receiving daily food with prayer and gratitude acknowledges God as Creator and turns ordinary meals into acts of worship. As food itself remains spiritually neutral, the believer must willingly limit personal freedom whenever it threatens another person's conscience.
•Idol sacrifices cannot alter the essential goodness of what God created, because false gods have no real existence or authority in the world.

Notes
•Pleroma (Fullness): The fullness of the earth encompasses all its animals, produce, and natural resources, none of which can be claimed or corrupted by false deities.
•Gar (For/Because): Citing Psalm 24:1, Paul uses this conjunction to ground the believer's freedom in market purchases directly in God's absolute ownership.

How will you receive God's gifts with gratitude today while using your freedom to build up others?

🇺🇸 TRUMP’S LATEST MOVES: MIDTERM ELECTIONS, SENATE SHOWDOWN AND A FRESH POLITICAL WARNING

WASHINGTON, October 27, 2026 | DETAILED POLITICAL REPORT

🇺🇸 Trump Intensifies Election Campaign as Republicans Face Growing Pressure

President Donald Trump has intensified his political campaign ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, throwing his weight behind Republican candidates while criticizing political opponents and pressing Congress to act on issues he says matter to ordinary Americans.

His latest publicly available statements from October 26 focused on Republican election prospects, Senate candidate endorsements, daylight-saving legislation and his campaign activities in Mississippi. These developments come as both parties compete to shape the final days of a closely watched election campaign.

ELECTIONS: TRUMP ENDORSES REPUBLICAN CANDIDATES

Trump publicly endorsed Republican candidates, including Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith of Mississippi and Michele Tafoya, who is running for the Senate in Minnesota. He also voiced support for Representative Clay Higgins of Louisiana.

In his message supporting Tafoya, Trump warned against alleged election irregularities and called for close scrutiny of ballot counting. He repeated his claim that he had previously won Minnesota but had been denied victory.

These remarks reflect Trump's continuing emphasis on election integrity and his willingness to make voting procedures a central campaign issue. However, his allegations about past election results should not be treated as established facts without supporting evidence.

MISSISSIPPI: TRUMP CAMPAIGNS FOR CINDY HYDE-SMITH

Trump traveled to Mississippi to campaign for Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith, whose reelection contest has attracted increased attention ahead of Election Day.

He praised the rally's expected turnout and encouraged supporters to vote for Hyde-Smith. The contest has become more competitive than Republicans had anticipated, with Democrat Scott Colom challenging the incumbent.

Trump's appearance underscores the importance of Republican efforts to retain their Senate majority. A difficult result in a traditionally Republican state could carry broader political significance for the party.

WASHINGTON: TRUMP DEMANDS ACTION ON DAYLIGHT-SAVING LEGISLATION

Trump criticized the US Senate for allowing legislation concerning daylight-saving time to stall.

He argued that Americans want more evening daylight and, above all, want to stop changing their clocks twice a year. He urged senators to hold a vote on the measure.

The House of Representatives previously approved the Sunshine Protection Act by a 308–117 vote, but the legislation remained stalled in the Senate according to the information cited in Trump's post.

The issue is relatively ordinary compared with the major national election debates, but it offers Trump an opportunity to present himself as advocating a practical change that affects millions of Americans.

POLITICAL STRATEGY: REPUBLICANS FACE A CRUCIAL TEST

Trump's latest endorsements and campaign appearances come at a decisive moment for his party. All 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 Senate seats are being contested in the 2026 midterm elections.

Republicans are attempting to defend their congressional majorities, while Democrats are seeking to capitalize on voter concerns about inflation, fuel costs, healthcare and the administration's policies.

Trump's involvement demonstrates that he is treating the election as a test of his political influence as well as a contest for congressional control.

WHAT HIS LATEST STATEMENTS SIGNAL

• Republican unity: He is using his endorsement to mobilize voters behind selected Republican candidates.

• Election scrutiny: He continues to raise concerns about ballot counting and alleged irregularities, making election administration part of his campaign message.

15-year-old Phillip Mullin from Alexandria, Louisiana, has made medical history by becoming the first child in the state to be declared functionally cured of sickle cell disease through groundbreaking gene therapy. After enduring more than 100 hospital stays throughout his childhood, Phillip finally received a life-changing treatment called Lyfgenia at Manning Family Children’s Hospital in New Orleans. Sickle cell disease is an inherited blood disorder that causes red blood cells to become abnormally shaped, restricting blood flow and triggering severe pain, organ damage, and potentially life-threatening complications. The innovative treatment uses the patient’s own blood-forming stem cells, which are genetically modified to help produce healthier red blood cells and reduce the painful complications associated with the disease. Phillip’s successful treatment represents a major milestone for pediatric healthcare in Louisiana and offers new hope to families facing similar medical challenges.

On October 23, 2026, Phillip and his family celebrated the remarkable achievement during an emotional ceremony at the hospital, recognizing his long journey from repeated hospitalizations to a future with significantly fewer limitations from sickle cell disease. After spending much of his childhood dealing with painful medical emergencies, Phillip now has the opportunity to enjoy everyday activities and pursue his dreams without the same constant fear of another sickle cell crisis. Inspired by his personal experiences, he has expressed a desire to become a hematologist-oncologist so he can help children and families battling serious blood disorders. Although being functionally cured does not necessarily mean the underlying genetic condition has been completely eliminated, the treatment aims to prevent severe sickle cell complications and dramatically improve quality of life.

 The Jews had significant competition in antiquity when  it came to worshipping Yahweh. Archeologists have discovered a  second great temple not far from Jerusalem that predates its better  known cousin. It belonged to the Samaritans, and may have been  edited out of the Bible once the rivalry had been decided.  Clad in gray coat, Aharon ben Ab-Chisda ben Yaacob, 85, is sitting  in the dim light of his house. He strikes up a throaty chant, a litany in  ancient Hebrew. He has a full beard and is wearing a red kippah on  his head.  The man is a high priest -- and his family tree goes back 132  generations. He says: "I am a direct descendent of Aaron, the brother  of the prophet Moses" -- who lived perhaps over 3,000 years ago.  Ab-Chisda is the spiritual leader of the Samaritans, a sect that is so  strict that its members are not even allowed to turn on the heat on the  Sabbath. They never eat shrimp and only marry among themselves.  Their women are said to be so impure during menstruation that they  are secluded in special rooms for seven days.  Outside, on the streets of Kiryat Luza, near Nablus, a cold wind is  blowing. The village lies just below the summit of Mount Gerizim.  There's a school, two shops and a site for sacrifices. This is home to  367 Samaritans. It's a small community.  Everyone here is required to attend religious services in the  synagogue on Saturdays. "Every baby boy has to be circumcised  precisely on the eighth day," says the high priest -- not beforehand,  and not afterwards.  EFTA_R1_00495829  EFTA01999637 22  Most important of all: the sect only believes in the written legacy of  Moses, the five books of the Pentateuch, also commonly known as  the Torah. They reject all other scripture from the Bible.  Once in the Majority  From a historical perspective, the Samaritans and the Jews have a  common lineage. The Old Testament recounts that 10 of the 12 tribes  in the region of Samaria founded the state of Israel in the year 926  BC. The two other clans lived farther south, in the mountainous  region of Judah, with its capital Jerusalem (see map).  In other words, the Samaritans were once in the majority. In ancient  times, there were 300,000 of them -- perhaps even over a million. But  their strictest law almost led to their downfall. It states: "None of you  may settle outside the promised land."  As a result, while the Jews fled across the globe to escape the cruelty  of foreign rulers, their relatives persevered in the land of their  forefathers and suffered under Byzantine tyrants and merciless  sultans. At the end of World War I, there were only 146 of them.  "Today we are doing better," says Ab-Chisda cheerily, as he gazes out  the window. Now, together with another group in Holon near Tel  Aviv, this religious community consists of 751 individuals.  But this population increase only took place because they broke with  age-old traditions and rescinded the ban against mixed marriages. In  2004, five Jewish women from Ukraine and one from Siberia, all of  them ready and willing to get married, were accepted into the  community.  Nevertheless, due to inbreeding, they have a wide range of genetic  defects. Trade journals have published studies on the forgotten  children of God. They often suffer from muscle weakness and Usher  syndrome, also known as deafblindness.  A Grim Fate  EFTA_R1_00495630  EFTA01999638 23  But their religion is alive and well. They all gather for Passover, a  holiday where the men wear white robes and perform a great animal  sacrifice.  During the ceremony, a priest cuts the throats of 50 lambs. Streams of  blood flow through a stone channel into a hole, where they are burnt  along with the intestines. The meat, which is cooked in a large  earthen oven, must be completely consumed during the night - otherwise it becomes unkosher.  But where do these archaic people come from?  It is a question that intrigues an increasing number of religious  scholars. Recent discoveries show that the Samaritans suffered a grim  fate. They were once the guardians of the Ark of the Covenant and  the keepers of the Mosaic tradition. But then they became the victims  of a smear campaign.  His hair windblown, Stefan Schorch stands in front of the synagogue  in Kiryat Luza. An expert on the Old Testament, Schorch hails from  the University of Halle-Wittenberg in eastern Germany and comes  here often -- usually armed with a tape recorder. He works like an  ethnologist would when studying a remote indigenous tribe.  Above all, Schorch is looking for sacred books.  It's 7:30 a.m., and a priest unlocks a small house of worship and  disappears into a niche behind a heavy red curtain. Inside stands a  safe filled with old volumes of the Pentateuch. "Unbelievable," says  the researcher, as he leafs through "a completely preserved edition  from the 14th century." He photographs each page of the tome. Then  the priest locks it away again.  'One Main Difference'  There was a time when nearly every affluent family possessed such a  precious handwritten book. Some of them reached Europe. Now, the  professor, who comes from the historic birthplace of Martin Luther's  Reformation, studies these texts, checking them line by line, and  EFTA_R1_00495631  EFTA01999639 24  word by word. And he compares the Samaritan Torah with the Jewish  version.  "Actually there's only one main difference," he says. Among the  Jews, Jerusalem is the world's religious epicenter, whereas for the  Samaritans it's Mount Gerizim.  But which Torah is the original? Until recently, the generally  accepted school of thought was as follows: In the fourth century BC,  the Samaritans split off as a radical sect. In the Bible, they appear as  outsiders and idol worshipers; they are evil. The parable of the "good  Samaritan" (Luke 10:25-37) offers a rather atypical portrayal of a  member of this sect.  The historian Titus Flavius Josephus, himself a Jew, mentions that  the apostates erected a shrine "in all haste" in the year 330 BC, as a  rather dilettantish attempt to emulate the Temple in Jerusalem.  Increasingly, though, it looks as though the Bible has handed down a  distorted picture of history. Papyrus scrolls recovered from Qumran  on the Dead Sea, as well as a fragment of the Bible that recently  surfaced on the market for antiquities, necessitate a "complete  reassessment," says Schorch.  The Site of the Original Temple  Yet the most exciting indication of how history actually transpired  has now been unearthed by Yitzhak Magen. Working behind security  fences, the archaeologist has been digging on the windswept summit  of Mount Gerizim.  His findings, which have only been partially published, are a virtual  sensation: As early as 2,500 years ago, the mountain was already  crowned with a huge, dazzling shrine, surrounded by a 96 by 98 meter (315 by 321-foot) enclosure. The wall had six-chamber gates  with colossal wooden doors.  At the time, the Temple of Jerusalem was, at most, but a simple  structure.  EFTA_R1_00495632  EFTA01999640 25  Magen has discovered 400,000 bone remains from sacrificial  animals. Inscriptions identify the site as the "House of the Lord." A  silver ring is adorned with the tetragrammaton YHWH, which stands  for Yahweh.  All of this means that a vast, rival place of worship stood only 50  kilometers (31 miles) from Jerusalem.  It is an astonishing discovery. A religious war was raging among the  Israelites, and the nation was divided. The Jews had powerful cousins  who were competing with them for religious leadership in the Holy  Land. The dispute revolved around a central question: Which  location deserved the honor of being the hearth and burnt offering  site of God Almighty?  Revising Holy Scripture  Researchers have a long way to go before they uncover all the details  of this conflict. It's clear, however, that it was extremely acrimonious.  Each side reviled the other. There was murder, mayhem and,  ultimately, even the Holy Scripture was revised.  At first -- so much is clear -- the Samaritans had the upper hand.  Indeed, compared with Jerusalem, Mount Gerizim enjoyed  significantly older rights: In the great tale of the history of the chosen  people, the mountain plays a key role.  Abraham, the progenitor of the Israelites -- who, according to legend,  roamed through the Orient as a shepherd around 1500 BC -- stopped  there because God had appeared to him in a wondrous vision. Later,  Jacob the patriarch traveled there to build the original shrine.  In the fifth book of Moses, the mountain summit finally earns a  prominent place in biblical history: After the flight from Egypt, the  Israelites wandered through the Sinai desert for 40 years. At last, they  reached the Jordan River from the east. Their old and weary leader  gazed across the river to the promised land, where "milk and honey  flow."  EFTA_R1_00495633  EFTA01999641 26  Shortly before his death, Moses issued an important command: The  people must first travel to Mount Gerizim. He said that six tribes  should climb it and proclaim blessings, while the other six tribes  should proclaim curses from the top of nearby Mount Ebal. It was a  kind of ritual taking possession of the promised land.  Finally, the prophet tells the Israelites to build a shrine "made of  stones" on Mount Gerizim and coat it with "plaster." Indeed, he said,  this is "the place that the Lord has chosen."  No Mention of a 'Chosen Place'  That, in any case, is what stands in the oldest Bible texts. They are  brittle papyrus scrolls that were made over 2,000 years ago in  Qumran, and have only recently been examined by experts.  In the Hebrew Bible, which Jerusalem's priests probably spent a good  deal of time revising, everything suddenly sounds quite different.  There is no longer any mention of a "chosen place."  The word "Gerizim" has also been removed from the crucial passage.  Instead, the text states that the Yahweh altar was erected on "Ebal."  "By naming the mountain of the curses," says Schorch, "they wanted  to cast the entire tale in a negative light, and deprive Gerizim of its  biblical legitimacy."  Schorch dates the intervention to around 150 BC. The researcher  stops short of calling it fraud, though, preferring to label it an  "adaptation of the Bible to their own religious view."  But why was this ruse ultimately successful? Why did the minority  win out? Didn't the opponent have the more populous country? A  palace already stood in their capital city, Samaria, in the year 1000  BC. Ivory has been found there. At the time, Jerusalem was still little  more than a village, with barely 1,500 inhabitants.  Researchers have solved this puzzle, and the answer even has a face:  It sports a curly beard and wears a bronze helmet. Starting in the year  732 BC, the Assyrians used their chariots to advance to the  EFTA_R1_00495634  EFTA01999642 27  Mediterranean and subjugate the state of Israel. The inhabitants were  either impaled or taken into captivity.  This devastated the country. The land of the Lord had been overrun  by violent hordes. Many fled to their cousins in Judah. Jerusalem's  population soared to 15,000.  Drinking and Whoring Heathens  Strengthened by this influx, the priests there decided it was time for  them to play the leading role in religious matters. Only a few years  after the invasion, King Hezekiah persuaded all Israelites -- Jews and  Samaritans alike -- to make a pilgrimage to Jerusalem. He said this  was the only place that still retained the freedom and purity to  worship the Almighty. The neighboring country was, of course,  occupied by drinking and whoring heathens.  To underscore their claim, the Jewish people wove an entire biblical  tale around their small, southern kingdom. According to this story,  around 1000 BC the biblical King David ruled from Jerusalem over a  glorious kingdom. His son Solomon allegedly built in the city a  temple made of cedar, "completely overlaid with gold." According to  the Bible, over 180,000 workers toiled to build it.  Total nonsense: Not a single shred of archaeological evidence has  ever been found to confirm the existence of Solomon's Temple.  The goal of the deception was clear, though: Judah's priests sought to  magnify the glory of their own city. And they passed up no  opportunity to vilify their rivals: In the Bible the Samaritans were  nearly always portrayed as unsavory characters. They were also said  to be ethnically impure because their blood had supposedly been  mixed with that of foreign colonialists.  The book of Ezra even recounts that these "enemies" tried to hinder  the reconstruction of the destroyed Temple of Jerusalem -- out of  pure envy, because they didn't have one of their own.  EFTA_R1_00495635  EFTA01999643 28  In reality, though, at that time, a shining divine fortress had already  stood for many years on Mount Gerizim. Magen, the archaeologist,  has discovered jewelry, silver, a fine cosmetics set and a small golden  bell from the splendid robe of a high priest.  Living in Peace  Around the year 180 BC, the ceremonial building grew to a size of  roughly 200 by 200 meters. The Samaritans added a monumental  staircase and rooms for "thousands of pilgrims." There were  apparently huge crowds of devout visitors. None of this is mentioned  in the Bible.  The dispute finally came to a head. In the year 128 BC, John  Hyrcanos, a Jewish prince, ascended Mount Gerizim with an army  and burned the proud sanctuary to the ground. Archaeologists have  found a "burn layer" along with arrow heads, swords, daggers and  lead missiles for slings.  The Samaritans never rebuilt their temple. From then on, the victors  wrote the (biblical) history books and forced their rivals into  oblivion.  And yet the "guardians of the law," as they call themselves, still exist  today. When Mark Twain visited the region in 1867, he encountered  the "sad, proud remnant of a once mighty community," which he  stared at "just as one would stare at a living mastodon."  Today, this astounding religious community is better off. They have a  seat in the Palestinian parliament and they maintain contacts with the  United Nations. "We want to live in peace with everyone," says the  high priest Ab-Chisda.  Despite their tragic history, the spiritual leader has not lost his sense  of humor. In response to the question as to what the Samaritan  paradise looks like, the old man hesitated briefly. Then, he said  mischievously: "It must be a wonderful place. Nobody has ever  returned to make a complaint."

Jeremiah 35-36 & Psalm 106 | October 27th | 2026 Global Bible Journey

Experience the Word of God in a new, immersive way.
It’s About Growth, Not a Checklist

As we continue through October 2026, remember that this journey is about genuine spiritual growth, not just "checking a box" for the day. Our goal is to let these scriptures transform our perspective and our priorities. If you missed a few days or are just joining us for the first time—don’t worry! Just jump right in with us today. The path to growth is always open, and there is no "behind" in this study.

Today’s Reading

In Jeremiah 35–36, the Lord uses the unwavering obedience of the Rechabite family—who faithfully keep the command of their ancestor not to drink wine—as a striking contrast to Judah's persistent disobedience toward the living God. In chapter 36, Jeremiah dictates the words of the Lord to Baruch the scribe, who reads the scroll aloud in the temple; however, when the scroll reaches King Jehoiakim, the king insolently cuts it with a penknife and burns it piece by piece in his winter fireplace, leading the Lord to command Jeremiah to take another scroll and write every word again, adding many similar words of judgment. Moving to the Psalms, Psalm 106 offers a sweeping historical confession and psalm of praise, acknowledging that "both we and our fathers have sinned." Tracing Israel’s repeated rebellion and idolatry from the Red Sea to the wilderness and into the Promised Land, the psalmist highlights the steadfast love and mercy of God, who repeatedly remembered His covenant, relented according to the abundance of His steadfast love, and heard their cry. This video is designed to help you focus on the text without distraction, featuring modern visuals and a clear, read-along experience.

Join the Global Community

This project is an outreach of the Richmond Church of Christ in Kentucky, connecting brothers and sisters from across the globe—including our communities in Nigeria, India, and South Africa. While our videos are "text-first," our teaching and discussions reflect the views we espouse at our local congregation.

Read With Us—Don't read alone!

We produce these videos at a moderate pace to allow for reflection. If you prefer to read faster or slower, click the Settings (Gear Icon) on this video player, select "Playback Speed," and adjust it to your liking (0.75x to 1.5x).

text:
Keep Charge of the Sanctuary

David Organizes the Levites for the Service of the House of the Lord

1 Chronicles 23 (ESV)

By Thomas Ohlendorf

Opening Scripture

When David was old and full of days, he made Solomon his son king over Israel. ... These were the sons of Levi by their fathers’ houses, the heads of fathers’ houses as they were listed according to the number of the names of the individuals from twenty years old and upward who were to do the work for the service of the house of the Lord. For David said, “The Lord, the God of Israel, has given rest to his people, and he dwells in Jerusalem forever. And so the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the things for its service.” ... Thus they were to keep charge of the tent of meeting and the sanctuary, and to attend the sons of Aaron, their brothers, for the service of the house of the Lord. (1 Chronicles 23:1, 24–26, 32 ESV)

Observation, Interpretation, Application

Observation. In his old age, full of days, David establishes Solomon as king and assembles the leaders, priests, and Levites. He numbers the Levites—38,000 from thirty years and upward (later adjusted to twenty)—and divides them: twenty-four thousand for the work of the house of the Lord, six thousand as officers and judges, four thousand gatekeepers, and four thousand to offer praises with the instruments he had made. He organizes them by the three sons of Levi—Gershon, Kohath, and Merari—recording their fathers’ houses. Aaron is set apart to dedicate the most holy things, to make offerings, minister, and pronounce blessings forever, while the sons of Moses remain among the Levites. Because the Lord has given rest and dwells in Jerusalem forever, the Levites no longer carry the tabernacle. Their duty is to assist the sons of Aaron: caring for courts and chambers, cleansing all that is holy, preparing the showbread and offerings, standing every morning and evening to thank and praise the Lord, and attending the sacrifices on Sabbaths, new moons, and feast days. In sum, they keep charge of the tent of meeting and the sanctuary and attend their brothers, the sons of Aaron.

Interpretation. This is not bureaucratic regimentation but divine scaffolding for the house of God. David acts under the Lord’s direction (cf. 1 Chronicles 28:19) to order worship according to the pattern of the Mosaic law, adapted to the permanent temple. The regulative principle is on display: worship is instituted by God himself and limited by his revealed will. The genealogies preserve the covenant continuity of the tribe set apart. The distinction between Aaronic priests and assisting Levites maintains the holiness of approach. The “rest” and permanent dwelling in Jerusalem point forward to the greater rest and the true temple. The shift from portable tabernacle to fixed sanctuary anticipates the once-for-all work of Christ, after which the church is the living temple in which ordered worship continues.

Application. The church today is called to the same ordered, Scripture-regulated worship. Officers and members serve in their distinct callings—teaching elders, ruling elders, deacons, and the whole congregation—assisting one another for the service of the house of God. Morning and evening praise, the Lord’s Day, and the ordinary means of grace are not optional ornaments but the appointed rhythm of thanksgiving. We keep charge of the sanctuary not by inventing new forms but by faithful attendance to the Word, sacraments, and prayer.

How Should We Live?

Live as those who have been given rest in Christ yet are still called to diligent service. Do not grow weary in the ordinary work of the church—preparing, assisting, gatekeeping the purity of the assembly, and lifting the voice of praise. Let every household and every member number himself among those who keep charge of the sanctuary.

Westminster Confession and Catechisms

Westminster Confession of Faith 21.1: “The light of nature showeth that there is a God... but the acceptable way of worshipping the true God is instituted by himself, and so limited by his own revealed will, that he may not be worshipped according to the imaginations and devices of men, or the suggestions of Satan, under any visible representation, or any other way not prescribed in the Holy Scripture.”

Larger Catechism 108–109 and 178–185 further instruct that we worship God only as he has appointed, and that the ordinary parts of religious worship are prayer, the reading and preaching of the Word, the singing of psalms, and the administration of the sacraments—precisely the ordered service the Levites were set to assist.

Historical Voices

Matthew Henry: “David, having given charge concerning the building of the temple, settles the method of the temple service, and orders the officers of it... When those of the same family were employed together, it would engage them to love and assist one another.”

John Calvin (on the necessity of reforming worship): God disapproves of all modes of worship not expressly sanctioned by his word. The organization of the Levites is therefore not David’s invention but the implementation of what the Spirit had given him for the glory of the Lord.

Christ in the Chapter

Aaron was set apart to dedicate the most holy things and to bless in the Lord’s name forever. Christ is the great High Priest who has entered the true sanctuary once for all by his own blood (Hebrews 9–10). He needs no assisting Levites to complete his work, yet he has made us a royal priesthood (1 Peter 2:9) and given the church officers and members who keep charge of the sanctuary of his body. The rest David proclaimed is fulfilled in the rest Christ gives to all who come to him (Matthew 11:28). The morning and evening praise of the Levites finds its perfect echo in the perpetual worship of the Lamb.

Closing Prayer

Lord God of Israel, who gave rest to your people and dwells among them forever, we thank you that in Christ the true temple has been raised and the true High Priest has finished his work. Grant us grace to keep charge of the sanctuary of your church with ordered, joyful, and obedient service. Number us among those who stand morning and evening to thank and praise you, and let our whole lives attend the service of your house, for the glory of Christ our King. Amen.

Reflection Questions

1. Where in your own life or in the life of your congregation is worship still being shaped by “the imaginations and devices of men” rather than by the revealed will of God?

2. How does the distinction between priests and Levites help us understand the different yet complementary callings of officers and members in the church?

3. In what concrete ways can you “keep charge of the sanctuary” this week—through prayer, service, purity, or praise?

text: Never? The US is massive with tons of subcultures, so it's wholly dependent where you are. If you're in the Ozarks (Missouri/Arkansas), never try to out-humble our generosity. Japanese like to try to express gratitude beyond what we tolerate and we find it very rude for people to out-thank us. We expect you to take food home with you both at restaurants and home dining and refusing it is rude. You'll be politely goaded into eating more than you can handle and it's fine to remain firm that your belly is stuffed, but you *must* eat dessert if dining at someone's house and they offer it. While not common practice in the Ozarks, sometimes apple pie comes with a slice of cheese on top, and it's rude not to eat it. We don't get too many foreigners here, so expect to be fawned over and slightly interrogated by locals whose only exposure to foreigners are the GODDAMN MEXICANS.

text:
@PeteHegseth COMMENDED THE CAVALRY FOR THIS BRUTAL SLAUGHTER OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLE!

FUCK @PeteHegseth 

DECEMBER 29, 1890 — WOUNDED KNEE — THE SNOW WAS RED
It was cold. So cold the guns froze to your hands.
Big Foot — Spotted Elk — was dying. Pneumonia. He was 64, lying in a wagon, wrapped in blankets, coughing blood. His people were carrying him. They had walked for days from the Cheyenne River because Sitting Bull had just been killed. They thought Pine Ridge would be safe because Red Cloud was there.
350 people. 120 men — old men, sick men. The rest — 230 — were women and children. Babies on cradleboards. Grandmothers who couldn't walk fast.
They had a white flag up. A white flag.
The 7th Cavalry surrounded them. The same regiment that lost to Sitting Bull at Little Bighorn 14 years before. The 7th Cavalry wanted revenge. They had been drinking all night.
They put four Hotchkiss guns on the hill. Those guns fired a 2-pound explosive shell every second. They pointed them down into the camp, into the tipis where children slept.
Morning. They told the men to come out and give up their guns. They went one by one. Yellow Bird, a medicine man, was doing the Ghost Dance prayer, throwing dust. He said the ghost shirts would stop bullets. The mothers believed it because they had nothing else to believe.
One man — Black Coyote — was deaf. He had a new Winchester. He paid $50 for it. He didn't want to give it away. Soldiers grabbed him. They spun him around. The gun fired into the air.
That was it.
One shot. Then hell.
At 10 feet away, the 7th Cavalry fired into the circle. Into men, into women holding babies.
The first volley killed half the men.
Then the Hotchkiss guns opened.
Imagine a shell that explodes. Now imagine it exploding in a group of women sitting on the ground holding their children.
The Lakota ran. They always tell you they ran. They didn't run to fight. They ran because their babies were screaming.
Mothers ran to the ravine — the dry creek — 200 yards away, a cut in the earth 10 feet deep. They thought the banks would save their babies. Soldiers stood on the top of the ravine and shot down into it.
You could hear the babies.
Girls — 12, 13-year-old girls — running, carrying their little brothers on their backs, shot in the back.
Old women — grandmothers — shot while holding their hands up. They found one old woman later, frozen, holding a white cloth.
Big Foot was in the wagon. They shot him. He was sick, he couldn't stand. They left his body in the snow.
When the shooting stopped, 25 soldiers were dead — killed by their own men shooting across the circle.
250 to 300 Lakota were dead.
But it wasn't over.
The wounded were left in the snow. It started to blizzard that afternoon. -30 wind. The Army left. They left the bodies and the wounded in the blizzard for three days.
On January 1st, a civilian burial party came. They found:
A baby, alive, under her dead mother in the ravine. She had been nursing her dead mother for three days in the snow. Her face was frostbitten black.
A boy, 3 years old, walking in circles, his dead mother frozen, his feet frozen solid. He didn't cry anymore.
Women, frozen in the position of holding their babies up — trying to offer them to the sky.
They dragged them with hooks. They threw them — men, women, babies — into one pit. 146 bodies in one pit. No ceremony. No names. Some were still breathing.
That pit is the monument you saw.
And then they sold pictures of it.
Photographer George Trager took pictures of the frozen bodies — twisted, piled. Northwestern Photo Co. printed them as postcards — "Battle of Wounded Knee — Bodies of Indians." White families bought them and sent them for Christmas. "Having a great time in Dakota."
In 1914, they went further. They hired survivors — Dewey Beard, who was a boy who hid under his dead father's body in the ravine and lived, and Turning Hawk — to act out their own families' murders for a silent film. For money. Because they were starving at Pine Ridge.
That is why there was a re-dedication in 1914. That is why a man named Miller was there selling postcards. The dead became entertainment.
TODAY
Go to Wounded Knee. It is quiet. Windy. No trees.
There are little fences around. Red cloth tied. Tobacco. Sage. Socks for babies who died with cold feet. Quarters left by veterans.
There are 300+ graves now. Veterans from Vietnam, Iraq, who died and wanted to be with their ancestors on that hill. Babies who died of pneumonia at Pine Ridge because there is no hospital.
And the boys — those Lakota boys who came to you — 16, 17 — they stand on that hill in the cold and tell white tourists: "This was a massacre, not a battle." They sell sage for $5 to feed their families. They memorize the names of the dead that the government never wrote down.
They remember, because America tried to forget.
Every December 29, in -30, Lakota ride horses 150 miles from Bridger to Wounded Knee. They don't ride for politics. They ride because Big Foot's people never finished their walk. They finish it for them.
They arrive at Wounded Knee at dawn on the 29th. They cry. They sing. They say the names.
The 7th Cavalry got 20 Medals of Honor for this.
The babies got a mass grave.
THE SNOW WAS RED THAT DAY. OUR MEMORY IS STILL WARM. 🩸

text:
🚨LAST NIGHT WAS A NIGHTMARE FOR OUR RESCUE. 
AND I AM ANGRY BEYOND MEASURE!

There are days when I wonder how much more one human being can be expected to endure in the name of compassion. Last night was one of those days.

Priya posted this morning about the situation with two new cats over at @gandolf_s, and I have a bit more to say.

It's a rant, and if rants aren't what you like to read, perhaps skip on by. But I make no apologies for my anger today. There comes a point when watching someone you care about being repeatedly taken advantage of, watching their kindness exploited and their sacrifices treated as though they mean nothing, becomes more than the heart can quietly bear. (I'm speaking of the community that contacts her for help)

Priya is sick. Again. (Flu, Covid, URI, not sure) She is in pain, exhausted, and should have been home in bed. She has appt to see her doctor tomorrow.

But when someone reached out to her, apparently through Nextdoor website, pleading for help trapping a cat at a gas station that they said they wanted to ADOPT, she did what she has done for so many years. She put the needs of a helpless animal ahead of her own...and went. It isn't often that she is asked to just trap and THEY will take the baby home! This is such great news for the babies and the rescue! 

The arrangement was simple. This person wanted the cat, had somewhere for it to go, and needed Priya's help catching it.
Except there wasn't one cat. There were TWO. Young siblings, surviving around a gas station, emerging from the darkness to search for scraps of food.

For three hours, in the cold, while feeling absolutely miserable, Priya worked to get them safely into a trap.
And she succeeded.

That's when the arrangement suddenly changed.

This person no longer wanted the cats. Not one. Not two. They weren't taking them home. They were leaving Priya standing there with two frightened animals in a trap and absolutely NOWHERE to put them.

And as a gesture of appreciation for her three hours of suffering and effort, this person offered to buy her a beverage from inside the gas station.

A BEVERAGE.

I cannot begin to tell you how disgusted I am.

Did it occur to this person, even for a moment, what they had just done? That a rescue might already be overflowing? That every available inch of space might be occupied? That there might be no money for another veterinary bill, another mouth to feed, another emergency?

Apparently not.

I'd like to give this person the benefit of the doubt, perhaps forgive their ignorance of how rescue works and what rescuers confront every day. That there isn't magical open space, and infinitely growing money tree in the yard. But I can't right now. I'm all out of "that's okay."

IT. IS. NOT. OKAY!

And now Priya has TWO MORE cats she has absolutely no room for!

With the recent arrival of five precious tuxedo kittens, we were already stretched beyond our limits. We have young ones needing spay and neuter surgeries, seven seniors needing medical attention, and a mountain of expenses we are struggling to meet.

In desperation, Priya had to call a friend in the middle of the night and beg him to take these two babies temporarily. He agreed to help, bless his heart, but he lives in an apartment where animals are not permitted.

That is not a solution. It is a temporary act of kindness that cannot last. Make no mistake. They are now her rescues and must bring them in ASAP as he cannot continue to house them.

And so here we are.

Two more innocent lives depending on a rescue that has nowhere to put them! A rescuer who is physically ill, emotionally exhausted, and being asked to find a solution to a crisis she did not create.

And the person responsible? Gone.

I sometimes think one of the cruelest parts of animal rescue isn't what happens to the animals. It's what people do to the human beings trying desperately to save them.

The dishonesty. The broken promises. The casual disregard for someone else's time, health, finances, and humanity.

People create these terrible situations, then walk away, leaving compassionate rescuers to clean up the mess. And because the lives involved are innocent, the rescuers cannot simply walk away themselves.

Compassion becomes the very thing that others take advantage of!

And that hurts my heart and makes me more angry than I can express.

Wednesday is Priya's birthday. I had hoped that our birthday cash match fundraiser, pinned to my page, would be a beautiful way to honor her years of service to the animals of Atlanta. A chance to give something back to a woman who has given so much of herself. 

I understand that times are difficult. We are all feeling the rising costs of simply getting through everyday life. But I had hoped we might come together to give Priya one lovely birthday surprise, a little financial breathing room and a reminder of how much her life's work means to others.

To everyone who has supported us, whether through a donation, a share, a kind word, or simply by cheering us on, thank you from the bottom of my heart. But please understand that we would never want anyone to put our needs before their own. Your well being and that of your loved ones must always come first. Whatever kindness you are able to offer, in whatever form it takes, helps us carry on.

I don't know how to make people understand what this woman endures. What rescuers endure. I have watched Priya sacrifice her own comfort, her financial security, her health, and so much of the life most of us take for granted, simply because she cannot bear to leave an animal suffering.

Friends, we desperately need your help.

We need ADOPTIONS. We need loving homes for the beautiful babies already in our care so that we can make room for these two new gas station wayfarers. We need help getting our five little tuxedo newcomers spayed and neutered so they, too, can begin their journeys toward forever homes.

Please don't let geography discourage you from considering adoption. We arrange transport to wonderful homes outside Atlanta. In just the past two weeks, one of our rescued cats went to a forever home in Boston, and two others went to Tennessee.
A loving home does not have to be around the corner. It just has to be the right home.

If you cannot adopt, please share our posts. If you can spare a few dollars, please consider contributing to Priya's birthday cash match, pinned to my page. I have a linktree in my bio. 
And if you know someone who has room in their home and heart for a rescued cat or two, please tell them about us.

I wanted Wednesday to be a celebration of this remarkable woman's life. Not another day of worrying about how she will manage to keep saving everyone.

And one last thing, to the person responsible for last night's fiasco...

To the absolute jackass who sat there watching a sick woman spend THREE HOURS in the cold trying to save two frightened little lives, only to wait until 3 AM, when they were finally safely trapped, to take pictures, announce you'd changed your mind for no apparent reason, and offer to buy her a damn Coke...

I hope someday you come to understand just how breathtakingly selfish, thoughtless, and downright slimy your behavior was. You took advantage of a woman's compassion, left her with a crisis she had neither the space nor the resources to handle, and walked away as though you'd done her a favor.

I hope life teaches you something about kindness, responsibility, and the consequences of treating decent human beings so disgracefully.

Because karma, as they say, has a remarkable memory.
Thank you for absolutely nothing, you rat bastard !

And now, back to the two innocent little lives who never asked to be caught in the middle of any of this.
💫If, by some miracle of fate, there is someone out there willing to foster these beautiful fuzzy wayfarers, it would be help sent by angels right now. We have no idea right now how "feral" they are. They need time and a slow approach to decompress. The expenses would be covered by the rescue. Vet, food. You add the time and love. If this is you, please reach out to me or Priya🙏

Please, friends. Let's give these two little wayfarers a future, and give Priya a reason to believe that the kindness she so freely gives to others will find its way back to her. ❤️
The Birthday Cash Match is a wonderful way to help. 🙏
